jordan: Quick ask — running into a perf regression where kernel selection seems to flip to a slower kernel for batched requests + KV churn. Need a tiny nsys checklist for a focused capture (no 30s monster).

maya: Mini checklist that worked for me recently: short warmup skip, then bracketed hot-window capture, include cuda+nvtx+osrt traces, avoid long sampling unless you need aggregate stats. Keep raw trace < 15s to keep file sizes small.

maya: Recommended flags (example):
```
nsys profile -o regress-kv.nsys \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=nvtx \
  --duration=12s \
  --sample=none \
  --force-overwrite \
  -- ./bench_infer.sh --batch-size=8 --requests=200
```
Put NVTX push/pop around: model forward, kv-get, kv-evict so timeline shows the exact spot.

lucas: If you need sampling (longer run) do `--sample=cpu` and lower sampling freq so events still visible. For kernel selection flips I prefer `sample=none` + a tight NVTX bracket so you capture full kernel timelines.

lucas: Quick tips to find kernel choice: in NSYS UI -> Timeline filter to GPU Kernels, show Kernel Name + Duration, then sort by name to spot different kernel variants (faster vs slower). Also snap GPU occupancy column.

maya: KV cache flow: add NVTX around kv_lookup/kvcache_evict, emit a small JSON log with hit/miss counts per request and correlate timing with kernel durations. If KV misses spike right before a slow kernel, likely data-dependent path causing different kernel codegen.

jordan: Good call — do folks prefer capture-range=nvtx vs capture-range=process?

lucas: Use capture-range=nvtx for precise bracket but ensure NVTX range is placed after warmup. If bracket misses a short spike, rerun with slightly earlier push. For flaky regressions try two captures: late warmup bracket (10s) and a longer sampled run for trends.

maya: One more: turn off unrelated system noise (disable perf collectors, docker stats) and pin threads/affinity if possible. If file grows too big NSYS will warn — infra-bot will post retention warnings.

infra-bot: :warning: Trace size limit approaching: keep duration <=15s for full cuda+osrt+nvidia traces to stay under 1GB. Use `--sample=cpu` for long aggregations or `--trace=cuda,nvtx` to drop osrt if needed.

jordan: Thanks! I'll add NVTX around kv ops and run the 12s bracket. Will paste the nsys snapshot when done. :thumbsup:
